title: [Perf Improvement] Skip returning rows on streaming subscription queries when there is no data
body:
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Yes. We have ~10k active streaming subscriptions in our system at any given time. The vast majority of the polling requests do not have any new data past the current cursor. New events arrive maybe once every 10 mins or so on average. Because Hasura returns 1 row no matter what per unique stream, Postgres is essentially sending back ~10k rows of empty data per second which eats CPU/Network IO.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Rather than returning "empty" rows like this in the streaming subscription query:

```
"result_id","result","cursor"
"893640e9-2088-4d30-a8ec-5eaf1aee6105","{""hasura_demo_events_stream"" : []}","{""id"" : null}"
```

If these were simply filtered out in the DB query and Hasura treated the missing row as effectively no data/cursor update which could save TONS of IO/CPU. In our case we'd go from sending back ~10k rows/s to likely only 1-5 rows/s max. I suspect many streaming subscriptions may have a similar access pattern.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Not aware of any alternatives.

comments.author: ecthiender
comments.body:
Hi @vincentjames501 , apologies for the late response.

The streaming subscriptions system is definitely not designed to send empty rows. If there is no data change, nothing is sent back.

We tried reproducing the issue on our end with a minimal setup, but we're unable to reproduce it.

![stream_no_bug](https://github.com/hasura/graphql-engine/assets/616387/394c79db-2dc3-4d89-b9df-b64ed47828b3)

Here, we have a single table with two rows. And only two data payloads were sent by the server. After that no data is sent.


Can you help us with a minimal setup where this can be reproduced? 

1. A minimal DB schema and sample data
2. Hasura metadata
3. The streaming subscription queries 

Let me know if you have more questions.

comments.author: vincentjames501
comments.body:
@ecthiender , the issue isn't data sent to the client over the websocket. The issue is the DB query from Hasura to Postgres (or underlying DB engine).


```
-- SCHEMA

CREATE SCHEMA hasura_demo;

CREATE TABLE hasura_demo.customer (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE hasura_demo.events (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id SERIAL NOT NULL REFERENCES hasura_demo.customer(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  event TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX hasura_demo_events_c_id ON hasura_demo.events(customer_id, id);

-- SETUP

INSERT INTO hasura_demo.customer (id, name)
SELECT i id, ('customer_' || i) name
FROM generate_series(0, 999) as t(i);

INSERT INTO hasura_demo.events (customer_id, event)
SELECT MOD(i, 1000) customer_id, ('event_' || i) name
FROM generate_series(0, 999999) as t(i);
```

Track these tables, add a new role with select permissions like the following:

![image](https://github.com/hasura/graphql-engine/assets/396866/37282650-c8d4-4fe3-9109-b4b1d37a6d47)

And then issue a GQL subscription request like the following:

```
subscription Events {
  hasura_demo_events_stream(batch_size:100, cursor:{initial_value:{id:123}}) {
    event
  }
}
```

It issues a query like this:

```
SELECT
	"__subs"."result_id",
	"__fld_resp"."root" AS "result",
	"__fld_resp"."cursor" AS "cursor"
FROM
	unnest(('{81fa7c1f-a9b7-4cd8-9264-48dc1cb258a1,893640e9-2088-4d30-a8ec-5eaf1aee6105}')::uuid[], ('{"{\"query\": {}, \"cursor\": {\"id\": \"999125\"}, \"session\": {\"x-hasura-customer-id\": \"124\"}, \"synthetic\": []}","{\"query\": {}, \"cursor\": {\"id\": \"999124\"}, \"session\": {\"x-hasura-customer-id\": \"123\"}, \"synthetic\": []}"}')::json[]) AS "__subs" ("result_id",
		"result_vars")
	LEFT OUTER JOIN LATERAL (
	SELECT
		json_build_object('hasura_demo_events_stream', "_hasura_demo_events_stream"."root") AS "root",
		to_json("_hasura_demo_events_stream"."cursor") AS "cursor"
	FROM (
		SELECT
			coalesce(json_agg("root" ORDER BY "root.pg.id" ASC), '[]') AS "root",
			json_build_object('id', (max("root.pg.id"))::text) AS "cursor"
		FROM (
			SELECT
				row_to_json((
					SELECT
						"_e"
					FROM (
						SELECT
							"_root.base"."event" AS "event") AS "_e")) AS "root",
				"_root.base"."id" AS "root.pg.id"
			FROM (
				SELECT
					*
				FROM
					"hasura_demo"."events"
				WHERE ((("hasura_demo"."events"."customer_id") = ((("__subs"."result_vars" #>> ARRAY['session', 'x-hasura-customer-id']))::integer))
					AND (("hasura_demo"."events"."id") > ((("__subs"."result_vars" #>> ARRAY['cursor', 'id']))::integer)))
			ORDER BY
				"id" ASC
			LIMIT 100) AS "_root.base"
	ORDER BY
		"root.pg.id" ASC) AS "_root") AS "_hasura_demo_events_stream") AS "__fld_resp" ON ('true');
```

Which returns something like this:

```
"81fa7c1f-a9b7-4cd8-9264-48dc1cb258a1","{""hasura_demo_events_stream"" : []}","{""id"" : null}"
"893640e9-2088-4d30-a8ec-5eaf1aee6105","{""hasura_demo_events_stream"" : []}","{""id"" : null}"
```

What I'm trying to get at in the original ticket is that for every multiplexed subscription we are returning rows from the DB even though they are "empty" as you can see by the empty array. These are indeed not send down over the websocket, but it creates a ton of IO between Hasura and the DB and is currently sending nearly 6k+ "empty" rows per second to Hasura.

If these were simply filtered out in the DB query and Hasura treated the missing row as effectively no data/cursor update which could save TONS of IO/CPU. In our case we'd go from sending back ~10k rows/s to likely only 1-5 rows/s max. I suspect many streaming subscriptions may have a similar access pattern.

comments.author: i-am-tom
comments.body: Hi @vincentjames501, https://github.com/hasura/graphql-engine/commit/0080e32e3c2b5cf67df8dfd032e4283912e77dfd should help you here - with the `remove_empty_subscription_responses`, we strip out all empty responses from database to server and from server to client. comments.author: vincentjames501
comments.body:
@i-am-tom I apologize for the super long delay here. But I'm not sure this is working as intended. If I rerun my example from this comment:

https://github.com/hasura/graphql-engine/issues/9994#issuecomment-2064301672

Using docker image: `hasura/graphql-engine:v2.45.1.cli-migrations-v3` on PG17 with:

```
      HASURA_GRAPHQL_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES: streaming_subscriptions, remove_empty_subscription_responses
```

I can confirm that Hasura sees the flag during startup:

```
...
enabled_apis":["metadata","config","pgdump","graphql"],"enabled_log_types":["startup","http-log","query-log","webhook-log","websocket-log"],"events_fetch_batch_size":100,"experimental_features":["streaming_subscriptions","remove_empty_subscription_responses"],"graceful_shutdown_timeout":60,"http_log_query_only_on_error":false,"infer_function_permissions":false,"jwt_secret":[],"live_query_options":{"batch_size":100,"refetch_delay":1},
...
```

But I don't see any difference in the query being sent to postgres. It's still returning:

```
"result_id","result","cursor"
"81fa7c1f-a9b7-4cd8-9264-48dc1cb258a1","{""hasura_demo_events_stream"" : []}","{""id"" : null}"
"893640e9-2088-4d30-a8ec-5eaf1aee6105","{""hasura_demo_events_stream"" : []}","{""id"" : null}"
```

where I would expect these rows to be removed from the response via the executed sql.

comments.author: vincentjames501
comments.body: To clarify, it seems like in this example if both hasura_demo_events_stream is empty and the cursor id isn't changed (NULL) then there is no point returning the row. Our prod db is doing ~20k+ rows/s essentially returning nothing useful and paying the network transfer cost and extra db cpu cost for the json serialization.

comments.author: vincentjames501
comments.body:
Ahhh. @i-am-tom , I think I see the issue. The fix was made for live query subscriptions -- not streaming query subscriptions which is what we're using. Using live queries I see this:

```
SELECT
	*
FROM (
	SELECT
		"__subs"."result_id",
		"__fld_resp"."root" AS "result"
	FROM
		unnest(('{3bedada0-c7be-4d52-9c0e-bdd2835c28f4}')::uuid[], ('{"{\"query\": {}, \"cursor\": {}, \"session\": {\"x-hasura-customer-id\": \"124\"}, \"synthetic\": [\"999125\"]}"}')::json[]) AS "__subs" ("result_id",
			"result_vars")
		LEFT OUTER JOIN LATERAL (
		SELECT
			json_build_object('hasura_demo_events', "_hasura_demo_events"."root") AS "root"
		FROM (
			SELECT
				coalesce(json_agg("root"), '[]') AS "root"
			FROM (
				SELECT
					row_to_json((
						SELECT
							"_e"
						FROM (
							SELECT
								"_root.base"."event" AS "event", "_root.base"."customer_id" AS "customer_id", "_root.base"."id" AS "id") AS "_e")) AS "root"
				FROM (
					SELECT
						*
					FROM
						"hasura_demo"."events"
					WHERE ((("hasura_demo"."events"."customer_id") = ((("__subs"."result_vars" #>> ARRAY['session', 'x-hasura-customer-id']))::integer))
						AND (("hasura_demo"."events"."id") > ((("__subs"."result_vars" #>> ARRAY['synthetic', '0']))::integer)))) AS "_root.base") AS "_root") AS "_hasura_demo_events") AS "__fld_resp" ON ('true')) AS "__multiplex"
WHERE (EXISTS (
		SELECT
			1
		FROM
			"json_each" ("result")
		WHERE ((json_array_length("value")) > ('0'))));
```

Which looks correct. Any chance this could get added to streaming subscriptions?

comments.author: rakeshkky
comments.body:
@vincentjames501 Thanks for letting us know the optimization isn't applicable to streaming subscriptions. 

After a careful look into the code, we could confirm the optimization is applicable to only live queries but not streaming subscriptions.

comments.author: vincentjames501
comments.body: @rakeshkky , thanks for the update. Should we reopen this ticket to have it addressed for streaming subscriptions? Or were you implying it was not possible to do? I'd be surprised if it isn't possible...

comments.author: jberryman
comments.body: @vincentjames501 just to be sure, in your subscription workload are you generally seeing responses from the database with 100 rows (the default batch size), or something much smaller? Just wanted to make sure since if the batches were only one or two rows, the savings relative to a "no rows" response wouldn't be very significant.

comments.author: vincentjames501
jberryman
comments.body: @vincentjames501 a fix was just merged so that `--experimental-features=remove_empty_subscription_responses` now correctly applies to streaming subscriptions, so that should go out in the next release

comments.body: @jberryman thank you! We'll try this out with the next release version and report back!
